question: Bez mletej červenej papriky si guláš ani paprikáš nevieme predstaviť. Z ktorého svetadielu však paprika pôvodne pochádza?
source_excerpt: The genus Capsicum originated in Central and South America. Mexico was probably the centre of origin of the chilli and sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum in the narrow sense).

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks treat red paprika as a core 'native' Central European spice (guláš, paprikáš, lečo), so they assume it is old and local or from Asia like pepper. In fact it came from the Americas and is relatively new to the region.
extra.verification_notes: Capsicum annuum originated in Mexico/Central America and was domesticated there, so the Americas is correct (https://uses.plantnet-project.org/en/Capsicum_annuum_(PROTA)).

explanation: Paprika rastie pôvodne v Strednej a Južnej Amerike a do Európy sa dostala až po Kolumbovi. Naše babičky ju teda varia „len“ niekoľko storočí.

question: Sušené púčiky, ktoré dávame do vareného vína a do medovníkov, dostali v slovenčine, nemčine aj angličtine meno podľa toho istého obyčajného predmetu. Akého?
source_excerpt: From Middle English clowe, from Old French clou de girofle, literally 'nail of clove'

extra.why_interesting: Everyone puts cloves in mulled wine or gingerbread but never notices that the name hides an ordinary household object. The player can work it out by picturing the dried bud's shape, and the fact that three languages chose the same comparison adds the 'huh, really?' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Cloves are named after nails in all three languages (Slovak klinček from klinec, German Nelke from Nägelein, English clove from French clou); I did not run a web search and relied on known etymology.

explanation: Klinček totiž vyzerá ako malý klinec s hlavičkou. Rovnako po nemecky Nelke pochádza z Nagel a anglické clove z francúzskeho clou. Pôvodne rastie na indonézskych Moluckách, na takzvaných Ostrovoch korenia.
